what_this_is: a pre-registered test of three stated beliefs about body type and infield position, not a shipping model
verdict_rule: SUPPORTED requires permutation p < 0.05 AND a 95% bootstrap CI clear of zero AND the sign the claim predicts

claims.claim: a short hitter is a poor first baseman, so height should rise with first-base share
claims.why: significant, interval clears zero, sign as claimed

claims.claim: an elite arm suits third base, so arm grade should rise with third-base share
a weak arm pushes a player to second base, so arm grade should FALL as second-base share rises
claims.why: significant, interval clears zero, sign as claimed

population: position players only; pitchers are excluded
caveats: FIRST-RUN ERROR, recorded rather than hidden: with pitchers left in, 55.4% of the height sample were pitchers, 2.0 inches taller on average and with no first-base innings, which produced a spurious H1 at p = 0.0005 in the WRONG direction. The zero-information control passed on that run: it validates the estimator, not the population.

Career innings share is an OUTCOME of club decisions, not a measure of ability. A club that believes the same folk wisdom will produce exactly this correlation whether or not the wisdom is true, so a SUPPORTED verdict here means 'clubs behave as if this is true', not 'this is true'.

Scouted arm grades are known to be confounded by throw context: the earlier arm gate measured a 1.94 mph context-adjusted spread against a 3.80 within-position SD, which is why raw arm-by-position was refused before.
OAA already contains arm and legs, so nothing here may be added to the positional fit as a bonus without double counting.
